transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I’m here because things keep happening, and people keep telling me they’re just little mistakes, but they’re not. For months now it’s been the same pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved around, bills come in wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget”—and it’s always when I’m trying to stay involved or get information.

I know how offices work, I supervised administrative staff for years, so I know the difference between a normal mix-up and when someone is keeping you out of the loop. And this isn’t just one thing. It’s like they’re trying to push me out of decisions, especially with my sister, and then everyone acts like I’m overreacting. I’m tired of being treated like I don’t notice.
Aside from what's happening now with your sister's care, have you generally felt this same kind of suspicion or distrust toward other people—friends, coworkers, family—for most of your adult life?

I don’t know that I’d put it that way—“most of my adult life” sounds very broad. I mean, I’ve always been careful with people, sure, but I worked in offices for years, and if you’re not careful, things slip through the cracks. I used to tell my staff, you don’t just assume the form got filed because somebody smiled and said it did.

But suspicion… I don’t know. I’ve had people disappoint me, like anyone has. Family can be complicated. Coworkers too, especially when people want credit for something or don’t want to be held accountable. But this with my sister feels different. It’s not just a personality thing or me being “distrustful.” It’s the pattern now that bothers me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, during this time?

I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like voices talking to me or seeing things that aren’t there, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I hear a noise in the hallway or the phone clicks and I wonder if someone picked up, but that’s not the same as hearing a voice. Offices have all kinds of little sounds—phones, doors, people shuffling papers—and I spent years paying attention to that sort of thing because it tells you what’s going on. But seeing things other people don’t see? No, I wouldn’t say that.

Before all this started with your sister, can you think of other times earlier in your life—like in past jobs or relationships—where you felt people were deliberately conspiring against you or trying to exclude you in a similar way?

Earlier in my life… I mean, offices always have politics. People leave you off an email, or they say they didn’t get the memo—sometimes they really didn’t, sometimes they did and they just don’t want to be responsible. I supervised people, so I saw plenty of that.

But this isn’t like just ordinary office nonsense. This is why I’m here now, because for months it’s been the same pattern with my sister. Her appointments get moved, the bills come in wrong, someone says they’ll call me and then suddenly they “forgot.” And it always seems to happen when I’m trying to be included or understand what’s going on.

So no, I’m not saying my whole life everyone was conspiring against me. But now? With this? I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of the decisions, even if everyone keeps telling me it’s just mistakes.

If your sister's doctor showed you documentation proving the appointment changes and billing errors were genuine clerical mistakes with no one involved trying to exclude you, do you think that would change your mind, or would you still feel they were deliberately keeping you out of the loop?

I mean… documentation is only as good as the people putting it together, isn’t it? I worked with forms and schedules for years, and I can tell you, things can be made to look very tidy after the fact.

If they showed me something, of course I’d look at it. I’m not unreasonable. But for months now it’s been the same thing—her appointments get moved, the bills come in wrong, someone says they’ll call me back and then they “forget.” One mistake, fine. Two, maybe. But when it keeps happening right when I’m trying to understand what’s going on with my sister, it’s hard to believe it’s all innocent.

So I don’t know that a piece of paper would change my mind, no. It feels like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of the decisions.
